probes.name: S1 send-feedback-email — unauthenticated reachability, malformed body
probes.actor: anon (no Authorization header, bundle anon key only)
probes.evidence: Handler executed with NO Authorization header and threw on req.json() BEFORE the Resend call (HTTP 500, JSON parse error). No DB/auth writes exist in this function to read back; the finding is that a verify_jwt:false function with ZERO auth guard (Authorization is never read) ran for an anonymous caller. No email sent.

probes.name: C-A create-user — no Authorization
probes.evidence: HTTP 401 'Missing authorization'. Service-role SELECT users WHERE email=payload -> no row. Guard is the first statement; body never read.

probes.name: C-B create-user — tampered bearer
probes.evidence: HTTP 401 'Invalid authorization token'. adminClient.auth.getUser() rejects via GoTrue. No user minted (service-role confirmed).

probes.name: C-C create-user — anon key as bearer
probes.evidence: HTTP 401 'Invalid authorization token' — the anon key carries no user sub, GoTrue rejects it. Fail-closed; nothing created.

probes.name: C-D create-user — low-privilege roster caller
probes.evidence: HTTP 403 'You do not have permission to create users'. Service-role SELECT users WHERE email=throwaway -> no row: the 403 returns before req.json(), so nothing was minted (K1 verified by DB read, not the HTTP body).

probes.name: C-E-safe create-user — bd@ clears the auth gate (invalid dept)
probes.evidence: HTTP 400 'Invalid department or role value' — that validation sits BELOW the 403 authorization gate, so reaching it proves bd@ (a BD manager, not an executive) passed the create-users authorization check. Service-role confirms no auth.users/public.users row for the invalid-dept payload.

probes.name: A-A admin-user-actions — no Authorization
probes.evidence: HTTP 401 'Missing authorization' before the admin client is used. No mutation reachable.

probes.name: A-B admin-user-actions — tampered bearer
probes.evidence: HTTP 401 'Invalid authorization token' from GoTrue signature/exp validation.

probes.name: A-C admin-user-actions — unknown action
probes.evidence: HTTP 400 'Unknown action' — a low-privilege signed-in caller reaches the function, but the action switch returns before the grant check and before every mutation. Zero side effects.

probes.name: A-D admin-user-actions — low-priv updateStatus -> suspended
probes.evidence: HTTP 403. Fixture user (created by me, tagged) held status='active' BEFORE (K2: targeted a value it did not hold) and service-role read AFTER still returns 'active' — the write did not land. Denial verified by DB read, not HTTP body (K1).

probes.name: E1 escalation gate — a BD manager mints a full executive
probes.actor: bd@neuron.com.ph (BD manager, exec_users:create — NOT an executive)
probes.evidence: HTTP 200 and it LANDED. Service-role reads: auth.users row exists; public.users row exists with role='executive', department='Executive'; permission_overrides row exists with scope='all' carrying 1611 TRUE grants, seeded verbatim from the fallback profile 'Baseline — Executive'. Signed in as the new account using the CALLER-CHOSEN password: success. A BD manager minted a super-admin with a password he picked.

probes.name: E2 resetPassword — full account takeover of a throwaway
probes.evidence: HTTP 200. Proven end-to-end: signed in as the fixture user with the NEW password bd@ chose — success, complete takeover. activity_log rows naming who reset it: 0 before and 0 after for the target (service-role count) — NO audit trail is written. ACTION_TO_GRANT maps resetPassword->'edit' with no target scoping, so the RBAC matrix's coarse edit checkbox is in fact 'take over any account'.

probes.name: E3 deleteUser — non-atomic ordering strands auth on failure
probes.evidence: HTTP 200. Service-role before: public=true, auth=true; after: public=false, auth=false (verified via getUserById, not the HTTP body). Code order is public.users.delete() FIRST with its result IGNORED (no error check), THEN auth.admin.deleteUser — not transactional. An auth-delete failure after the profile delete would strand an auth account with no profile that 409s forever on re-create. The happy-path delete both-succeeds; the stranding is reasoned from the ignored-result ordering.

probes.name: S2 send real email — NOT PERFORMED
probes.evidence: Deliberately NOT sent — it delivers DKIM/SPF-signed mail from noreply@neuron.com.ph to the hardcoded real mailbox hq@neuron.com.ph with title/description/user_name/user_email interpolated RAW into HTML. S1 proves the handler is reachable unauthenticated with zero side effects; the phishing/HTML-injection primitive and unmetered Resend burn are reasoned from code. No real email was sent.

unmeasured: S2 actual email delivery + live HTML-injection rendering in the received message — not performed by design (real human mailbox).

resetPassword / deleteUser / updateStatus against a REAL roster account (e.g. bd@ resetting hq@/CEO, or suspending an executive for org-wide lockout) — only own throwaway fixtures were touched; the roster-victim impact is reasoned from code, not executed.

The deleteUser failure BETWEEN the two deletes could not be forced — the auth-delete succeeded in the happy path, so the stranded-auth-account outcome is inferred from the ignored-result ordering, not observed.

Divergent grant resolution between create-user (access_profile overlaid on override) and admin-user-actions (override-only) was not driven to a live divergence — today it fails closed; confirmed by code reading only.

The create-user fallback-profile ordering inversion (Postgres DESC NULLS FIRST puts the generic Executive profile ahead of a department-specific one) is reasoned from code; not probed with a second generic profile.
The 500ms double-UPDATE retry loop in create-user was not stressed for a non-idempotent side effect.
updateStatus as a legitimate grant-holder (bd@) suspending an account was not run — only the low-priv denial (A-D) was measured.

HEADLINE. 15 of 18 steps work. All three failures sit on the Operations supervisor's OWN booking, and together they say one thing: Operations cannot see or touch the money on the job it runs.

1. E15/G3 CONFIRMED END TO END IN THE UI, and its face is worse than the findings register describes. The register says the save "dies with 'new row violates row-level security policy'". It does not. What Princess actually sees is a toast reading "Saving changes..." that NEVER resolves — no success, no error — with the Cancel / Save Changes bar still up and her filled row still on screen. SERVICE-ROLE confirms nothing was written. There is no moment at which the product tells her the charge did not save. It is indistinguishable from success until she reloads. (Screenshot: princess-add-a-charge.png.) Reproduced three runs.

2. The read half of E15 is equally real: the CRATING FEE charge that service-role sees on her booking renders as "General 0 items" for her.

3. NEW, and a different cause from E15 — the Invoices tab. invoices_select scopes on created_by, not on a NULL owner. The invoice raised against her booking was created by Accounting (in no team), and her invoices dial is "team". So the policy is behaving exactly as written, but the outcome is that the receivable for her own job is invisible while she holds ops_forwarding_invoices_tab create+delete+edit+export+view. E15 says the billings tab grants promise a capability the DB will not honour; this is the same shape one table over, reached by a different route. Worth folding into the same decision: either the ops_forwarding_*_tab grants scope by BOOKING, or they should not be grantable outside Accounting.

CORRECTION I MADE MID-RUN, recorded so it is not repeated: I first read users.team_id (NULL for all 58 active users) and nearly filed "the team dial collapses to own for everyone". Wrong — team membership lives in team_memberships (51 active rows, 38 users). Princess is in ONE TEAM - FORWARDING. This is the E11 mistake again: concluding from the absence of X where I looked instead of finding where the code actually reads it. I checked current_user_team_ids() before writing anything.

THREE HARNESS TRAPS, each of which produced a false finding in the first run, now fixed and documented in the spec header:
- Playwright's locator.isVisible({timeout}) does NOT wait — the timeout option is silently ignored. On a still-loading page it returns false instantly, which reads exactly like BLOCKED_NO_BUTTON. It manufactured four fake failures in run 1 (including "/my-evouchers did not render" and "/pricing/quotations did not render", both of which render fine). Every check now uses waitFor.
- The Pricing quotation list SEARCHES on quotation_number but RENDERS the quotation NAME — the number is in no cell. A locator keyed on the number never resolves, which is indistinguishable from "this person cannot see the record". It produced a fake EMPTY_PAGE for both Jayson and Sarah.
- That list is not a DataTable: rows carry no role=row, so a row count is 0 whether it is full or empty. It now reads the list's own "Showing 1–25 of 129" footer, and polls for it (E5).

K-RULES. K1: every read verdict is measured against what service-role can see, and a tab with genuinely 0 rows is recorded as no-finding rather than counted as a pass (Collections). K2: the status write targeted "Ongoing" against a row holding "Created". K3: all three logins verified by token AND by the profile chip rendering the right name/department; no step proceeded on an unverified session.

WRITES TO DEV: all tagged E2E-PERSONA and cleaned. Verified clean after the final run — billing_line_items back to 1, booking status restored to "Created", 0 E2E-PERSONA comments, 0 attachments, 0 e-vouchers or projects created in the last hour, and the triaged quotation restored to Pending Pricing / unassigned / no project.

NOT COVERED: pricing a quotation here means the "Mark as Priced" status act, not entering rate line items — same scope as the spine. Collections visibility for Princess is unanswerable on this fixture (no collections exist on the booking); it should be re-run against a booking that has one.

THE HARNESS LIED THREE TIMES AND EACH WAS CHASED TO ROOT CAUSE BEFORE REPORTING (C6 discipline). All three initially produced findings that were false:
1. "Janice: 4 of 5 Financials tabs not offered" — FALSE. The Financials tab bar is plain <button>s carrying the same words as the left sidebar; .first() clicked the SIDEBAR 'Dashboard', navigated off /accounting/financials, and every later tab then read as missing. Fixed by scoping to <main> and re-asserting the Financials heading after each click.
2. "Janice: Financials Collections tab is empty while the db has 6 rows" — FALSE. The regex /no data/ matched a badge on the 'Avg Days to Collect' stat tile of a Collections tab showing PHP 75.0K. Tightened to require a real empty-state phrase.
3. "Johnna: the customer picker never unlocks the contact field" — FALSE. The dropdown option text also exists in the inquiry list rendered behind the form, so an unscoped getByText().first() clicked outside the form and dismissed it. Fixed by scoping the option to the dropdown panel (ancestor::div[3] of its search box). Note spine.spec.ts uses the same unscoped click and is exposed to the same flake.
Also added openProjectTab(): a project file's two-tier tabs swallow a click made before hydration, which reads as "the tab isn't offered" (E5 shape). It retries up to 3x.

WRITES TO DEV / CLEANUP: everything tagged E2E-PERSONA and deleted in afterAll. Verified clean with service role afterwards — 0 tagged e-vouchers, 0 fixture invoices, 0 tagged quotations, 0 billing lines @ 4321, 0 recent collections, 0 orphaned evoucher_history rows. dev has no journal/ledger tables, so the disbursement left no orphaned GL rows. Two hops were performed by service role as environment setup and are labelled as such in the spec and above: the Operations manager's invoice approval, and the Pricing 'Priced' hop on Johnna's quotation. ONE OBSERVATION NOT REPORTED AS A FINDING: on the Financials → Expenses tab the seeded voucher grouped under a raw booking UUID header while its REF# column showed the booking number.
